name: kerryback-public
description: Public plugins: a reviewer for work Claude produced, a narrated-video builder for slide decks, a personal literature knowledge base, free financial and economic data, WRDS research data, two-stage DCF valuation, risk parity portfolios, and one-on-one tutors that coach a student to the answer.

plugins.name: critique
plugins.description: Critique work Claude produced and say what to do about it. Parallel reviewer agents -- correctness traced back to the files that produced each number, clarity, and a devil's advocate that reads the code -- then Claude argues against its own reviewers and publishes an HTML guide that leads with the verdict and lays out the paths forward. Heavyweight: it fans out multiple subagents.

plugins.name: voiceover
plugins.description: Turn a slide deck into a narrated MP4 video plus a transcript. Give it the PDF of your slides and Claude writes the narration; a local app shows each slide beside its script, where you edit it, pick an ElevenLabs voice, and generate. The MP4 and transcript are saved to your working directory.

plugins.name: litdb
plugins.description: Personal literature + notes knowledge base: hybrid keyword+semantic search over your papers and notes, Zotero/Better BibTeX import, loose-PDF folder ingestion with full text, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar discovery, and a citation graph. Local-first; the runtime installs into ~/.litdb on first use.

plugins.name: finance-data
plugins.description: Fetch free financial, market, and economic data (prices, fundamentals, SEC filings, macro series, asset-pricing factors) from Yahoo, Stooq, SEC EDGAR, FRED, Ken French, FinnHub, FMP, and US Treasury, and save it as CSV.

plugins.name: wrds
plugins.description: Empirical asset-pricing data from WRDS (CRSP v2/Compustat) and Open Source Asset Pricing: extractable Python building blocks for connect (without a 2FA prompt), pull, merge, market cap aggregated across share classes, the CRSP-Compustat link, book equity, accounting alignment and firm age — every query run against live WRDS. Surfaces the constructions that are genuine decisions rather than common practice (Ken French vs Drechsler's WRDS script vs OpenAP, and the 4- vs 6-month reporting lag) instead of picking silently, and ships twelve WRDS reference scripts.

plugins.name: two-stage-dcf
plugins.description: Two-stage enterprise valuation from a company's financial statements and text, fetched for a ticker (statements and 10-Ks from SEC EDGAR, press releases from 8-Ks, call transcripts from the Motley Fool) or read from a folder. Classifies every reported balance-sheet line and foots it, computes the historical driver ratios with a script, reads the MD&A, transcripts and press releases for evidence on each driver, and writes one HTML page with four tabs: Line items (the classification), Forecasts (the argument for each assumption with quoted citations), an editable Baseline grid, and DCF, which revalues in the browser as the Baseline is edited, with a measured ranking of what moves the answer. The numbers live in a CSV that rebuilds the page, so the assumptions can be argued over and revised; when they are settled it delivers an Excel workbook whose model is live formulas, with sensitivity and driver-ranking sheets and a Check sheet that goes red if the formulas ever disagree with the Python engine.

plugins.name: risk-parity
plugins.description: The risk parity (equal risk contribution) portfolio and the covariance matrix it needs, from historical returns, prices, or a covariance matrix: long-only weights in which every asset supplies the same share of portfolio variance, with each asset's risk share and inverse-volatility weight alongside.

plugins.name: tutor
plugins.description: One-on-one tutoring skills. Each skill coaches a student through a piece of course material by handing them problems and diagnosing their answers rather than presenting worked solutions. Currently ships binomial option pricing (replicating portfolios, risk-neutral probabilities, backward induction, early exercise) and agency law (actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, liability on the contract). Install once and every tutor in the collection is available as /tutor:<subject>.
